trayIcon.description: Show a notification-area icon. The process stays resident either way; with false it is simply invisible.

iconSize.description: Icon edge length in logical pixels at 100% scaling. Scaled per monitor DPI (16 -> 24 at 150%, 32 at 200%).

theme.description: auto follows Settings > Personalization > Colors and updates without a restart.

anchor.description: taskbar pins the menu flush against the taskbar edge while following the cursor along it. cursor opens at the exact pointer position, like menuApp.

language.description: UI language for the tray menu, notifications and dialogs -- not your menu entries, which always show whatever label you gave them, and not the special catalog (English by design). "auto" detects the Windows display language at startup; an explicit tag (e.g. "de") forces it regardless of the system locale, and "en" forces English even where a translation exists. Looks for lang/<tag>.json next to the exe, then an embedded copy, then falls back to English -- never a hard error.

launchers.description: Standalone, pin-to-taskbar entries, separate from the menu items. --launch <id> runs one directly (what a pinned shortcut calls); --make-launcher / --make-launchers write .lnk files to drag onto the taskbar. Each click starts a new instance and the launcher never becomes a running-app entry.

label.description: Display text. Required for everything except separators.

type.description: Unknown values are skipped with a warning rather than failing the file, so a config written for a later build still opens.

exec.description: An .exe, a document, a folder, a URL or a .lnk. Anything that is not an executable is opened with its registered default handler: .xlsx in Excel, a folder in Explorer, https:// in the browser. Supports %VAR% environment references. For a Microsoft Store app use appId instead.

appId.description: AppUserModelID of a Microsoft Store (packaged) app, launched via shell:AppsFolder — for apps that have no .exe to point at. Find it with PowerShell's Get-StartApps (lists Name and AppID for every Start-menu app), or browse them in explorer shell:AppsFolder. Example: "Microsoft.Windows.Photos_8wekyb3d8bbwe!App". Mutually exclusive with exec (appId wins if both are set). The icon resolves automatically to the app's package logo; set icon only to override it.

special.description: A built-in Windows target named by a short id — Device Manager, Task Manager, Windows Update, the Recycle Bin and so on. A third way to name a target, alongside exec and appId (special wins if more than one is set). label and icon are supplied from the catalog, so { "special": "taskManager" } is a complete entry; set either to override. Run TaskbarMenu.exe --list-specials to print the catalog. Unknown ids are skipped with a warning rather than failing the file.

args.description: Arguments as separate strings; quoting is handled automatically. Ignored for document targets, where the handler decides. Supports %VAR%.

icon.description: An .ico path, or "file,index" to pick one icon out of an .exe/.dll that holds several (a negative index is a resource id). May also be an image file — .svg, .png, .jpg, .gif, .bmp, .tiff, and .webp/.avif/.heic where the OS codec is installed — which is scaled to the icon size with its aspect ratio preserved (a non-square image is centered on transparency, not stretched). Omit to let the shell resolve the icon from exec. Use --list-icons and --pick-icon to find an index.

elevated.description: Launch via the runas verb, producing a UAC prompt.

tooltip.description: Reserved; native popup menus have no tooltips yet.

confirm.description: Only meaningful on a power special (lock, signOut, sleep, hibernate, restart, shutdown). Defaults to true for the actions that close your applications — signOut, restart and shutdown — and to false for the reversible ones. Set false to act immediately on a single click, or true to make even locking ask.

folder.description: Turns the entry into a submenu listing this directory's contents, read when the submenu is opened rather than at startup — so it always shows what is there now. Supports %VAR%. The submenu leads with an "Open <label>" item. Mutually exclusive with exec, appId, special and items.

depth.description: How many directory levels a folder submenu descends. 1 lists the folder and opens subfolders in Explorer; 2 and above turn subfolders into submenus of their own, each read only when opened. Values above 20 are clamped with a warning.

limit.description: Maximum entries shown per level of a folder submenu. Anything beyond it is replaced by a clickable "More…" entry that opens the folder in Explorer. Values above 2000 are clamped with a warning.

items.description: Turns the entry into a submenu at any depth. exec is ignored when present.

openAll.description: Only meaningful alongside items. Adds an "Open all" entry above the submenu's own entries, with a separator below it, that launches every launchable entry in the submenu with one click -- recursing into nested submenus, but not into a folder/special submenu whose contents are only discovered when opened, and skipping power actions.

id.description: Stable key. --launch <id> resolves it and the generated shortcut's AppUserModelID is derived from it, so the pinned button survives regeneration. Do not change an id once a launcher has been pinned — that mints a new pin. Also the .lnk file's base name.

label.description: Display text for the shortcut. Optional; --launch also accepts a label as a fallback key when no id matches.

exec.description: An .exe, a document, a folder, a URL or a .lnk, opened with its registered default handler. Supports %VAR%. For a Microsoft Store app use appId instead.

appId.description: AppUserModelID of a Microsoft Store (packaged) app, launched via shell:AppsFolder. Mutually exclusive with exec (appId wins if both are set).

special.description: A built-in Windows target named by a short id, as for a menu entry — so a launcher can pin e.g. Device Manager to the taskbar. label and icon are supplied from the catalog. Run TaskbarMenu.exe --list-specials to print it. Mutually exclusive with exec and appId (special wins).

args.description: Arguments as separate strings; quoting is handled automatically. Supports %VAR%.

icon.description: Shortcut icon as an .ico path or "file,index" into an .exe/.dll (a negative index is a resource id). Image files and Store-app logos cannot be used as a shortcut icon; the target's own icon is used instead. Omit to let the shell resolve it from exec.

elevated.description: Launch via the runas verb, producing a UAC prompt.

show.description: Initial window state of the launched target.

confirm.description: Only meaningful on a power special. Same defaults as a menu entry: true for signOut, restart and shutdown, false for lock, sleep and hibernate.
